'''Vera Isabella Furness''' {{Post-nominals|country=UK|MBE}} (2 June 1921 –2002) was an English chemist and industrial manager who worked for [[Courtaulds]] in Coventry and later [[Campsie, County Tyrone|Campsie]] from 1953 to 1981. She worked on the production of the acrylic Courtelle and developed a copolymer that would allow for a more successful commercial dying of the filter. Furness then incorporated a reagent into the process giving it a near white fibre. She was appointed [[Order of the British Empire|Member of the Order of the British Empire]] (MBE) in 1971.

==Biography==
She was born in [[Birmingham]] on 2 June 1921.<ref name="25000Entry">{{cite encyclopedia|title=Furness, Vera (1921–2002)|url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/women/dictionaries-thesauruses-pictures-and-press-releases/furness-vera-1921-2002|encyclopedia=[[Dictionary of Women Worldwide|Dictionary of Women Worldwide: 25,000 Women Through the Ages]]|date=2006|accessdate=25 April 2021|via=Encyclopedia.com|archive-date=20 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210120145616/https://www.encyclopedia.com/women/dictionaries-thesauruses-pictures-and-press-releases/furness-vera-1921-2002|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="SP1970">{{cite news|last=Dallas|first=Zoë|title=With Women's Liberation|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76447803/zoe-dallas-25-august-1970-starphoenix/|work=[[StarPhoenix]]|date=25 August 1970|accessdate=25 April 2021|page=4|via=Newspapers.com|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Furness originally studied to become a teacher at a [[Normal school|teacher training college]] and went on to become a secondary school teacher.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last1=F. Rayner-Canham|first1=Marlene|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aCZqDQAAQBAJ&q=Vera+Isabella+Furness&pg=PA513|title=Chemistry was Their Life: Pioneering British Women Chemists, 1880–1949|last2=Rayner-Canham|first2=Geoff|publisher=[[Imperial College Press]]|year=2008|isbn=978-1-86094-986-9|location=London, England|pages=513|chapter=Women Chemists in the 1940s – Vera Furness}}</ref> She studied for an external chemistry degree at the [[University of London]] whilst teaching full-time at Birmingham Central Technical College (today [[Aston University|Acton University]]).<ref name="25000Entry" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name="IWSEntry" /> Following her graduation from the university with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1946 in which she did a doctoral thesis on hexomethylenetetramines with dialkylanilines and phenols,<ref name="25000Entry" /> she was appointed [[BX Plastics]]' development chemist,<ref name=":0" /> where she conducted research for her [[Master of Science]] degree.<ref name="IWSEntry" /> Furness' thesis concerned with preparing [[Quinolone antibiotic|fluoroquinolones]] mono-substituted in the benzene ring.<ref name="IWSEntry">{{cite book|editor1-last=Haines|editor1-first=Catharine M.C.|editor2-last=Stevens|editor2-first=Helen M.|title=International Women in Science – A Biographical Dictionary to 1950|chapter=Furness, Vera I.|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HftdjMNDvwIC&q=Vera+Furness+chemist&pg=PA107|year=2001|publisher=[[ABC-CLIO]]|location=[[Santa Barbara, California]]|pages=107–108|isbn=1-57607-090-5}}</ref>

Furness declined the offer of a full-time teaching job after finishing her [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in 1952 and went back to industrial research because she felt that was where her interest was.<ref name=":0" /> She joined [[Courtaulds]] in [[Coventry]] in 1953,<ref name="25000Entry" /> and worked on producing Courtelle, an acrylic, and then developed a copolymer that would allow for a more successful commercial dying of the filter.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="IWSEntry" /> She subsequently incorporated a reagent into the process, giving it a fibre that was nearly white. Furness was fully involved in every aspect of the process such as chemical and mechanical issues.<ref name="IWSEntry" /> She went to China, Poland, and Soviet Union to talk about the process of acrylic plants and the technical production before the plants were built.<ref name="25000Entry" /><ref name="IWSEntry" /> After the [[Royal Aircraft Establishment]] discovered the best fibre precursor as Courtelle in 1963 when it was developing carbon fibers for improved aircraft components, Furness took part in making the fibre better and made a process for producing it on a mass scale starting from 1965.<ref name="IWSEntry" /> She was head of the Acetate and Synthetic Fibres Laboratory from 1964 to 1969.<ref name="25000Entry" />

She led a section with 100 employees and was the first women to hold such a professional industry position over males in such a division in England.<ref name="SP1970" /><ref name="IWSEntry" /> Furness was asked to lower energy consumption across each of the 400 sites in the United Kingdom during the oil crisis and did so by establishing objectives based on production.<ref name="IWSEntry" /> She was appointed general manager of Courtaulds Research Division in their factory in [[Campsie, County Tyrone]] and held the position from May 1970 to 1976.<ref name="SP1970" /><ref name="IWSEntry" /> Between 1976 and 1978, Furness served as chair of Steel Cords.<ref name="25000Entry" /> Following her move to [[Northern Ireland]] to become manager of Courtaulds' Campsie factory in 1978, she was on multiple boards and committees such as [[Enterprise of Ulster|Enterprise Ulster]]; the Labour Relations Agency conciliator; the Northern Ireland Economic Council; the University of Ulster Council and the [[Education in Northern Ireland|Western Education and Library Board]].<ref name="IWSEntry" /> She left Courtaulds in 1981.<ref name="25000Entry" /> Furness was also company director of Roe Valley Community Property from 28 July 2000 to 8 June 2002.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vera Isabella Furness|url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/officers/MvT6IQIRMHK8epgsUASnoYc9YUw/appointments|access-date=25 April 2021|publisher=[[Companies House]]}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 1971, she was appointed [[Order of the British Empire|Member of the Order of the British Empire]] (MBE) "for services to export".<ref name="IWSEntry" /><ref>{{London Gazette| issue = 45384| date = 12 June 1971| pages = 5966| supp = y}}</ref> Furness died in 2002 in [[Limavady]], close to [[Derry]], Northern Ireland.<ref name="25000Entry" />
